title: Orchestrator + Gateway + Adapter territory cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
A compact reference for decisions and handoffs between API gateway, orchestrator (control plane), and runtime adapters. This is a lightweight working note to clarify responsibilities when we design routing policies and multi-region failover chains. Not finished — working assumptions + open questions included.

Scope / Intended audience:
- Platform engineers making changes to routing, rollout, or runtime adapters
- SREs owning region failover and oncall runbooks
- Solutions engineers coordinating Dedicated / Private model variants

High-level separation (one-liners):
- API Gateway: ingress, auth, request shaping, edge-level rate limits, and route metadata. Does not make long-term routing decisions; tags requests with flow metadata.
- Orchestrator (control plane): policy evaluation, model selection, region/capacity routing, rollout strategies, and cross-service fallbacks. Maintains canonical routing policies and rollout state.
- Runtime Adapters: per-hardware model bindings, capacity reporting, local admission control, and model variant compatibility checks. Exposes a small RPC surface for orchestrator to query capacity and push config.

Routing policy primitives (vocabulary):
- primary: route first attempted (usually low-latency region + preferred model).
- fallback chain: ordered list of compatible endpoints (region/model variant) to try on failure or slow path.
- tier: hosting tier label (hosted, dedicated, private) used by cost/capacity policies.
- latency_budget_ms: SLO window controlling when orchestrator will attempt speculative fallback.
- capacity_score: normalized 0..100 value from runtime adapter indicating headroom.

Ownership sketch (who changes what):
- Gateway team (eng-api-gateway): owns edge filters, auth integrations, feature flags that change ingress shaping. Maintains mapping between public routes and internal flow IDs.
- Orchestrator team (eng-platform-orchestrator): owns routing policy evaluation, rollout APIs (canary/AB), multi-region decision engine, and policy DSL. Responsible for policy migration scripts.
- Runtime adapters (eng-serving-runtime & eng-private-deploy): own adapter binary, capacity reporting, per-model descriptor format (.model.json), and node-level admission. They must commit adapter version compatibility records.
- Console / Product (product-console): owns visualization of routing decisions and rollout dashboards but does not modify policies directly.

Boundary rules (non-ambiguous defaults):
- Anything that affects per-request routing decision beyond the current request's headers belongs to orchestrator. Gateway can provide hints/metadata but not make final fallback decisions.
- Adapter-level admission control (rejecting a request due to memory pressure) is local; adapter must emit standard error codes so orchestrator can interpret and trigger fallback.
- Auth & tenant-scoped quotas are enforced at gateway edge OR orchestrator depending on token freshness; for short-lived tokens gateway handles initial enforcement, orchestrator validates for internal routing.

Multi-region failover pattern (recommended canonical flow):
1. Gateway receives request; injects flow_id, tenant_priority, client_region_hint.
2. Orchestrator evaluates policy: preferred region(s) (latency-first), model variant constraints, tenant isolation (dedicated pools), and capacity_score thresholds.
3. Orchestrator returns target runtime endpoint and expected trace_id; gateway proxies request to chosen endpoint.
4. At runtime: adapter returns either success, recoverable error (e.g., busy/kv-cache miss), or terminal error (model mismatch).
5. On recoverable error or latency_budget breach, orchestrator attempts next entry in fallback chain; gateway receives updated instruction and retries transparently (idempotency flag required).

Capacity & admission contract (adapter => orchestrator):
- periodic heartbeat (15s) with capacity_score and max_concurrent_inflight.
- on-demand snapshot: orchestrator can call /v1/adapter/capacity to get full slot map for scheduling.
- standard errors: BUSY_RETRYABLE, UNAVAILABLE, MODEL_MISMATCH, AUTH_FAILURE. Each maps to orchestrator policy paths.

Operational ownership & alerts (quick map):
- Latency SLO breach (edge->region mismatch): primary alert to orchestrator oncall, paging gateway oncall on correlated error rates.
- Adapter OOM / node drain: page runtime-adapter oncall; orchestrator should start draining flows away from impacted pool.
- Canary rollout regression (per-eval thresholds exceeded): page product and orchestrator owners; rollback via orchestrator API.

Runbook excerpts (short):
- If a region reports capacity_score < 20 for > 3 minutes: orchestrator marks region as low-capacity, starts rerouting traffic to fallback chain; create incident with "region-capacity" tag.
- If adapter returns MODEL_MISMATCH for > 0.1% of requests in 5m: strip that variant from rollout and start variant-health job.

Cross-team integration contracts (must-have):
- Gateway -> orchestrator: route metadata spec (YAML) + change window reviews.
- Orchestrator -> adapter: schema for model descriptor + compatibility matrix. Backwards compatibility: orchestrator must accept adapters implementing older descriptor v1 for 6 months after v2 release.
- Deployment cadence: adapters 2-week release window; orchestrator infra changes require 2-week QA and one canary window in test region.

Open questions / tradeoffs (we need decisions):
- Should tenant isolation always prefer dedicated pools even if cost is higher? (Current draft: prefer dedicated only if tenant_priority >= 80 or explicit contract).
- Gateway vs orchestrator rate limiting split for bursty traffic from the same tenant across regions. We need a detailed example flow and simulated cost model.
- How to surface cold-start latency from private deployments in orchestrator policy (we currently only have capacity_score which conflates cold-start and sustained capacity).

Immediate action items (next 2 sprints):
- [ ] Draft ATA (adapter telemetry augment) RFC: add cold_start_ms and mean_latency_1m to heartbeat. Owner: Arjun. Due: 2025-02-01.
- [ ] Add failure-code-to-policy mapping to orchestrator test harness. Owner: Lena. Due: 2025-01-20.
- [ ] Run region-failure chaos experiment using canary traffic (test region): verify fallback chain completes within latency_budget_ms=200. Owner: Dmitri. Due: 2025-02-10.

Decision log pointers (quick links):
- routing-policy-dsl: CONFLUENCE-INF-57 (draft)
- adapter-error-codes: GH PR #812 (see linked_artifacts above)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally compact; the goal is a single-page working reference you can pin in a planning meeting. If you need diagrams, see CONFLUENCE-INF-57 or ping me for a whiteboard session.
- Prefer concrete examples when arguing for policy changes (cost vs latency table for a real tenant).

Signed-off-by: Maya Chen (mchen@redwood.ai)
